lessons.title: What does it mean for a machine to learn?
lessons.outcome: You can say what it means for a machine to learn. You fit a line by hand, let the computer fit it, and test both lines on new points.

lessons.title: The gradient
lessons.outcome: You can find the gradient of a loss by nudging a weight. You know which way a training step moves the weight, and why its learning rate must not be too large.

lessons.title: Gradient descent with many parameters
lessons.outcome: You can find the gradient of a loss with two weights by nudging each weight alone. You can explain how one step changes both weights, and why a learning rate that is too large makes the loss grow.
widgets: three learning rates on the map

lessons.title: The neuron and the layer
lessons.outcome: You can compute the output of one neuron from its inputs, weights and bias. You can explain why a layer of many neurons is one matrix product, and count its parameters.
lessons.code:
nn::Linear layer(784, 32);   // W (32, 784), b (32)
Variable y = layer(x);       // x (B, 784) → y (B, 32)

lessons.title: Activation functions
lessons.outcome: You can explain why two layers without an activation function act like one layer. You can show how ReLU neurons, as hinges, bend a straight line into a curve, and why a small sigmoid gradient slows learning.
lessons.code:
Variable h = relu(z);      // max(0, z)
Variable s = sigmoid(z);   // 1 / (1 + e^-z)

lessons.title: Two classes and the decision boundary
lessons.outcome: You can explain how a model sorts points into two classes. You can see why hidden neurons let the decision boundary bend.

lessons.title: Softmax and cross-entropy
lessons.outcome: You can turn the scores of a model into probabilities with softmax. You can explain cross-entropy as the surprise at the right class, and why it beats the squared miss for classes.
lessons.code:
Variable p = softmax(logits, 1);      // each row: probabilities that add to 1
nn::CrossEntropyLoss ce;             // the surprise at the right class
Variable L = ce(logits, labels);     // logits (B, 10), labels (B)

lessons.title: How the computer finds every gradient at once
lessons.outcome: You can explain why it is too slow to find each gradient by nudging one parameter at a time. You can follow the chain rule backward through a small network, and say why TorC adds gradients.
widgets: the graph lab, one value with three uses

lessons.title: Why deep networks are hard to start
lessons.outcome: You can explain why two neurons that start equal stay equal, and why the gradients can fade in a deep network. You can say why TorC starts the weights with the spread √(2/in).

lessons.title: The training loop
lessons.outcome: You can explain why each training step uses a small random batch, and why its gradient is only an estimate. You can compare two batch sizes fairly and follow the five lines of the training loop.

lessons.title: Better optimizers
lessons.outcome: You can explain how momentum, Adam and AdamW change the step of plain gradient descent. You can say why a fair comparison gives each optimizer its own best learning rate, and why no optimizer wins on every problem.
widgets: plain SGD and momentum in a valley
a fair race on two problems

lessons.title: Does it work on new data?
lessons.outcome: You can tell how much a model overfits from its training and validation miss. You can choose when to stop with a validation set and measure the final model once on a test set.

lessons.title: Digits with an MLP
lessons.outcome: You can train a network that reads handwritten digits and count its mistakes. You can say which digits it mixes up, and why.

lessons.title: One training step from start to end
lessons.outcome: You can follow one training step on one digit, from the pixels to the changed weight. You see the probability of the right digit go up.

lessons.title: Convolution
lessons.outcome: You can explain how a small pattern detector slides over an image. You can count the weights of a convolution layer and find the size of its output.

lessons.title: Digits with a CNN
lessons.outcome: You can explain why a convolutional network reads the same digits with fewer weights than the first network for digits.

lessons.title: From digits to ChatGPT
lessons.outcome: You can explain how a language model such as ChatGPT learns to predict the next token with the loop of this course. You know where TorC stops and where to learn more.

lessons.title: Tensors
lessons.outcome: You can read the shape of a tensor in TorC. You can predict the result of broadcasting, of a sum along an axis and of a batched matrix product.

lessons.title: Modules
lessons.outcome: You can build a TorC model from Module and Sequential. You can list its parameters and explain the rule for the forward cache.

lessons.title: Common errors in TorC programs
lessons.outcome: You can find the cause of the most common errors in TorC programs. You can read the error messages that TorC gives.

lessons.title: The symbols of this course
lessons.outcome: You can look up each symbol of this course, with its name and the lesson that introduces it.

lessons.title: Glossary
lessons.outcome: You can look up each term of this course, with a short definition in plain words.

lessons.title: Backprop lab
lessons.outcome: You can run small calculations forward and backward, and see where each gradient comes from.
